fixtures.name: logcat_choreographer_jank
fixtures.command: adb shell logcat -d -v threadtime | grep Choreographer
fixtures.description: Real Choreographer jank: 'I Choreographer: Skipped N frames!  The application may be doing too much work on its main thread.' TWO spaces after the exclamation mark, and the tag carries the janking app's own pid in the logcat columns -- unlike the ActivityManager ANR lines, whose pid is system_server's. Recorded because every skipped-frame test in this repo built its input from an f-string, which proves only that the parser matches the f-string. Provoked by a cold start and then AnrReceiver's 40s block, and what lands differs by level. emulator-api35 recorded the block's own line, 'Skipped 2401 frames', and 2401 * 16.7ms is 40.1 seconds -- the first independent check this repo has that the FRAME_MS heuristic tracks wall-clock, on a stall whose real length is known. emulator-api33 recorded no line for the block, only the cold start's (tens of frames), plus a Looper 'Slow dispatch' line the grep keeps because it names Choreographer. A cold start janks only when the host happens to be busy, so how MANY lines land here is not fixed; the severity-boundary tests vary the frame count off this line rather than typing new ones.

fixtures.command: adb -s <serial> logcat -B -T 1, stopped by the recorder after 5 s
fixtures.description: What a live `logcat -B -T 1` delivers in 5 s on a device left alone, before its reader stops it; the recorder writes nothing to the device. On API 33 (Android 13) it delivers nothing: logcat writes `-B` records through stdio and flushes only after a TEXT record (AOSP system/logging logcat.cpp, android13-release), so records wait in its 4 KiB buffer and are lost when the stream is terminated. On API 35 each record arrives as it is logged. Manifest: every chunk the stream delivered, timed (`stream`), and how many of the window's records it had delivered by the stop (`window`).

fixtures.name: logcat_strictmode_violation
fixtures.command: adb shell logcat -d -v threadtime | grep -E '[VDIWEF] StrictMode: '
fixtures.description: What StrictMode actually logs, against what anr_pipeline was written for. The real header is 'D StrictMode: StrictMode policy violation; ~duration=27 ms: android.os.strictmode.DiskReadViolation'; the invented sample was 'D StrictMode: Slow operation detected on main thread', which StrictMode prints in no form at all (it borrows the wording of ActivityManager's own 'Slow operation:' bookkeeping, a different subsystem entirely). Two consequences visible in this file. The violation states its OWN duration, which _classify_anr discards in favour of a hard-coded WARN_FRAMES * FRAME_MS. And every frame of the stack trace that follows is logged under the same StrictMode tag, so a tag-only match turns one violation into one event per stack frame -- about thirty. Provoked by StrictModeActivity, which enables the policy and then reads and writes a file on the main thread.

fixtures.description: `pm grant --user <secondary user>` of CAMERA, a runtime permission the fixture app requests: what a per-user grant that WORKS prints and its exit status (stdout and stderr together, then the echoed `exit=`), ground truth for privacy_manager's --user handling. That it took effect for that user only is in dumpsys_package_two_users, recorded in the same run; manifest `secondary_user`, `permission`.

fixtures.name: pm_grant_user_missing
fixtures.command: adb shell 'pm grant --user <id not in pm list users> com.example.composefixture android.permission.CAMERA 2>&1; echo exit=$?' (in pm_grant_user_not_requested's run)
fixtures.description: `pm grant --user <id>` for a user the device does not have (manifest `missing_user`): nothing printed and exit 0 (measured, API 33). Neither the output nor the status says the user is missing, so privacy_manager checks the id against `pm list users` before granting.

fixtures.name: pm_grant_user_not_requested
fixtures.command: adb shell pm create-user v9-fixture-tmp; pm list users (pm_list_users_two_users); pm grant --user <missing id> ... (pm_grant_user_missing); pm grant --user <id> com.example.composefixture android.permission.CAMERA; dumpsys package com.example.composefixture (dumpsys_package_user_not_installed); pm install-existing --user <id> com.example.composefixture; pm grant --user <id> com.example.composefixture android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS; pm grant then pm revoke --user <id> com.example.composefixture android.permission.CAMERA; dumpsys package com.example.composefixture (dumpsys_package_user_revoked); pm remove-user <id>
fixtures.description: `pm grant --user <secondary user>` of a runtime permission the fixture app does NOT request (POST_NOTIFICATIONS), the app installed for that user: `java.lang.SecurityException: Package ... has not requested permission ...` and a stack trace on stderr, exit 255 (API 33). On API 35 the same grant for user 0 is a silent exit 0 (emulator-api35 pm_grant_not_requested), so a reader must handle both. The throwaway user is removed in the same run and its removal read back; manifest `secondary_user`, `permission`.

fixtures.name: pm_list_users
fixtures.command: adb shell pm list users
fixtures.description: `pm list users` on a device with only its system user: a `Users:` line, then one tab-indented `UserInfo{<id>:<name>:<flags>}` row per user, `running` after a started one. Ground truth for privacy_manager's check that a --user id exists before it grants (pm_grant_user_missing: a grant for a missing user exits 0).

fixtures.name: pm_list_users_two_users
fixtures.command: adb shell pm list users (in pm_grant_user_not_requested's run)
fixtures.description: `pm list users` while a throwaway secondary user exists: `UserInfo{0:...}` and `UserInfo{<id>:...}` rows (the id is the manifest's `secondary_user`). Ground truth for parsing more than one user out of the listing.

fixtures.name: pm_revoke_permission_echo
fixtures.command: adb shell pm revoke --user 0 com.android.settings 'android.permission.<echo text>'
fixtures.description: pm_grant_permission_echo for privacy_manager --revoke / --reset: the same exception, the name printed back on stderr, exit 255.

fixtures.name: ps_all_pid_uid
fixtures.command: adb shell ps -A -o PID,UID
fixtures.description: `ps -A -o PID,UID`: every process, as the two numeric columns parse_ps_uids reads (a `PID UID` header, then one row per process). Ground truth for a whole-table pid -> uid read rather than ps_pid_uid's `-p` subset. Manifest `system_server_pid` (`pidof system_server` right after) names the row that must read uid 1000.

fixtures.name: ps_pid_uid
fixtures.command: adb shell ps -o PID,UID -p <fixture app pid>,<system_server pid>
fixtures.description: `ps -o PID,UID -p <pid>,<pid>`: a header, then one row per pid that exists, sorted by pid, with the NUMERIC uid (10205 for the fixture app, 1000 for system_server). Measured: `-p a -p b` answers the same; a pid that does not exist is left out, and with none existing only the header prints and the exit status is 1. The pids are under 'pids' in this entry.

fixtures.name: run_as_cat_fixture_db
fixtures.command: adb shell -T run-as com.example.composefixture cat /data/data/com.example.composefixture/databases/fixture.db
fixtures.description: container.py's --cat read of the fixture app's databases/fixture.db: a binary file, read by the same argv as run_as_cat_utf8_cap and written byte for byte. Its first byte that is not valid UTF-8 is early in the SQLite header, so it is binary whole and binary when capped anywhere past that byte; forgiving the character a cap cuts must not forgive this. emulator_only only because a capture callable reads it; it changes nothing.

fixtures.name: run_as_cat_utf8_cap
fixtures.command: adb push <70161 bytes of UTF-8 text> /data/local/tmp/aes_utf8_cap.txt; adb shell -T run-as com.example.composefixture cp /data/local/tmp/aes_utf8_cap.txt /data/data/com.example.composefixture/files/aes_utf8_cap.txt; adb shell -T run-as com.example.composefixture cat /data/data/com.example.composefixture/files/aes_utf8_cap.txt
fixtures.description: container.py's --cat read (`adb shell -T run-as <pkg> cat <absolute path>`) of a UTF-8 text file longer than its 65,536-byte cap, pushed into the fixture app's files/ for the purpose and removed after. Mixed-script lines (German, Japanese, accented Latin), with the header padded so the cap cuts a three-byte character after its second byte (manifest: cap_bytes, split_character_starts_at). Written byte for byte and refused unless it is exactly the file pushed. Slicing to the cap and strict-decoding the slice calls this file binary: the only invalid bytes are the incomplete character the cut itself made.

fixtures.name: setprop_locale_echo
fixtures.command: adb shell setprop persist.sys.locale '<echo text>'
fixtures.description: appearance --locale with <echo text> (see pm_grant_permission_echo): refused, exit 1, and `Failed to set property 'persist.sys.locale' to '<value>'.` prints the value back on STDERR, newline and all, so the forged line starts a line of the stderr run_adb classifies. The property reads `com.example.app1` in the file: the aliaser takes `persist.sys.locale` for a package name (departure 2).
